title: Mbappe's France Faces Morocco in a World Cup Rematch Full of History
summary:
Get ready for a huge soccer showdown! On Thursday, France will play Morocco in the World Cup quarterfinals at Foxborough Stadium near Boston. This is a rematch of the 2022 World Cup semifinal, where France beat Morocco 2-0. But a lot has changed since then.

France has been the best team in the tournament so far, playing exciting, attacking soccer. Their superstar Kylian Mbappe has already scored seven goals—that's tied for the most in the tournament! He scored the winning penalty in their last game, a tough 1-0 victory over Paraguay. France also has Ousmane Dembele, who scored three goals in one game earlier. They're loaded with talent.

But don't count out Morocco! They're no longer just a surprise team. They cruised through their group with a draw against Brazil and easy wins over Haiti and Scotland. Then they crushed Canada 3-0 in the round of 16. Their coach, Mohamed Ouahbi, says, "We're no longer a surprise today, and that's a great source of pride." Morocco has a star goalkeeper, Yassine Bounou, and one of the best right-backs in the world, Achraf Hakimi. They play tough defense and work together as a team.

There's extra meaning to this game because Morocco was once a French colony, and many people of Moroccan origin live in France. Coach Ouahbi says revenge isn't the main goal—they just want to make their people proud. But beating France would be extra sweet.

France showed they can win ugly too, grinding out a 1-0 win against a physical Paraguay team. Morocco will try to frustrate France's stars. It's a clash of styles: France's flashy attack vs. Morocco's stingy defense. Who will move on to the semifinals?
why_it_matters: Even if you don't play soccer, this game shows how sports can connect different countries and histories, and that hard work and teamwork can take you far.

Soccer (called football in most countries) is the world's most popular sport, with billions of fans.
